contributions.statement: For aggregation over corpora larger than one context (for example tagging thousands of content items), a parent agent can write a script that fans out per-chunk subagents and aggregates their outputs deterministically, but measure token cost first, since the reported gain over a single coding agent is against a copied baseline and vanished at 4M tokens.
contributions.evidence: §4.2 Table 1: 81.36% vs 71.75% (Codex baseline copied from Cao et al., not re-run); Table 3: 66.7% at 4M against 71.75% and below baseline in 4/13 buckets (audit); §4.5 admits no token/latency instrumentation.
relative_to: Recursive Language Models (RLM) / map-reduce over chunks

reason: A named variant of recursive subagent fan-out with an uncontrolled baseline and no cost data; it is worth trying for bulk content processing, not as evidence.
